current.title: Coffee Just Hit $4.41 A Pound — A Record
current.hook: Your coffee habit is about to get pricier.
current.closing: Drink it slow. It earned that price.
current.question: Have you noticed your coffee getting more expensive? Tell me below.

segments.topic: how high coffee prices have climbed
segments.say: Arabica coffee futures hit $4.41 a pound in February 2025, the highest price ever recorded. Back in 2019 it was around $1.05. The climb wasn't steady, it was a series of shocks.
The shock is Brazil's drought. One trade house cut its Brazil arabica forecast from 45.4 million bags to just 34.4 million, an 11-million-bag hole in the world's biggest coffee supply overnight.

segments.topic: how much coffee prices have doubled
segments.say: That's why your cup costs more than it did a year ago. $2.00 a pound in February 2024. $4.41 by February 2025. More than double, in twelve months.

judge.one_line: Competent and clean-ish, but it opens on a slow bar build instead of a hook, leans on charts and stock machines for a story that begs to be made of coffee, and puts text under the mascot and under a mark in three places.
problems: The hook is the thing the rubric names first: hook@0.3 to hook@2.2 (t=0.30-2.20s) is a bar chart filling in behind caption words — a slow chart build, no event, no reason to stay.
hook@0.3 (t=0.30s): the caption 'Your coffee' is set straight across the 2019 row, covering that row's $1.1 value; on a phone the top row is unreadable for the first second.
seg1:mid/seg1:end (t=11.61s/16.26s): the pink polyline floats with no axis or baseline, disconnected from the range pill below it, and reads as a decorative scribble rather than a price path.
seg1:mid (t=11.61s): '$4.4' at the end of 'anywhere between $1.1 and $4.4' is behind the mascot's torso.
seg1 does not demonstrate its own line — the script says 'a series of shocks' and the picture shows one dot resting inside a span.

seg2:start (t=21.95s) abandons its best idea: the coffee-cup waffle (each = 2M) is the only subject-made image in the video and it is replaced by a generic line chart for the actual 45.4M to 34.4M cut.
fixes: Open on the shock, not the axis: start at seg1's content — the price jolting up in one visible hit with a hard sound-shaped move in frame 1 — and let the 2019-2023 history arrive after the viewer is held.
Never print a caption over a data row: reserve the caption band below the source line, or push the chart's top row down so hook@0.3's 'Your coffee' cannot land on 2019's value.

Rebuild seg1 as a coffee-made shock ladder: a cup or bean column whose level jumps once per shock (2021 frost, 2024 drought) and holds between jumps, anchored to a baseline that uses the empty lower third; delete the floating polyline and the range pill.
Keep the cup waffle and make it the seg2 mechanic end to end: let 11M bags' worth of cups (2M each) physically empty out of the grid to land 34.4M, instead of cutting to a line chart.
Move the mascot's anchor out of every text band — offset him to the opposite side of any active label, so seg1's '$4.4' and the seg2 caption are never occluded.
Lift the Feb-2024 value off its pan: set it above or beside the slab in ink on the ground, not on the mark, at seg4.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'. Write answer_path as one JSON object matching answer_schema, request_id and slug copied, and commit it. Do not touch the request.
